cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward: coal is the primary fuel and is bought in bulk, primarily imported Indonesian coal, through three routes - from Indian importers after the coal has cleared Indian customs, on a 'high seas basis' (purchased while in transit at sea, with the Company then responsible for customs clearance), and directly from overseas suppliers on a CIF basis with the Company clearing customs. Coal price is based on or linked to the fluctuating international price of coal. This bulk coal position is monetised in two directions: it fuels the boilers, and the excess is sold in the open market as a coal-trading line that was 28.14% of revenue from operations in H1FY26 and 19.30% in Fiscal 2025 (an invoice-only / purchase-order business with no fixed coal supply contracts). Purchase geography (state-wise bifurcation of raw materials): Gujarat 1,643.57 million / 99.99% in H1FY26, 2,728.56 million / 96.23% in Fiscal 2025, 1,700.86 million / 78.19% in Fiscal 2024 and 2,064.71 million / 88.64% in Fiscal 2023, with the balance from Dadra & Nagar Haveli, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and outside India. Fuel is being progressively diversified away from coal into non-fossil sources - plastic waste, textile chindi, agro-waste, refuse-derived fuel, waste gas and textile waste - with the 15 TPH Vapi WTE unit already commissioned on non-fossil fuel and Nandesari (Phase 2), Vapi (Phase 3) and Pirana (Ahmedabad) planned on non-fossil fuel; at Pirana the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation supplies the waste-dumping-site land, half the capex and a 347.50 million subsidy under a 10-year work order. Distribution pipe is sourced domestically. Utilities: power is drawn from the local state power grid plus captive electricity from back-pressure turbines at Nandesari, with turbines planned at other locations. Quality control begins at procurement with high-GCV coal in the 3,217-5,204 KCal range; hydrated lime is sprinkled on coal to cut SOx, and fly ash is disposed of per state pollution-control requirements. Forward: the Company owns, operates and maintains the entire distribution layer - a 56,236 meter operational pipeline system as of November 15, 2025 (55,916 m at September 30, 2025, up from 27,085 m at March 31, 2023), running on pipeline rights-of-way easements and connecting into customer-owned pipes at the customer's premises, with individual pipelines spanning 3,000 to 20,000 meters. Real-time monitoring uses flow meters, SCADA, steam traps/auto valves, third-party sensor and data-visualisation providers over a custom API and SQL database, and drone mapping for leak detection; emissions parameters (SPM, SOx, NOx and, for waste-fired boilers, HCl) are tracked. Customers control their own offtake via site valves without disturbing the generating system. A deliberately capital-light forward variant is the 'purchase and distribution' model, in which the Company buys unused or by-product steam from third-party industrial units and distributes it through its own pipelines - already in place with Kilburn Chemicals Limited, at Dahej GIDC, and at Sachin GIDC with Group Company Sanjoo Dyeing and Printing Mills Private Limited, which owns the generation assets while the Company operates and maintains those boilers and distributes the steam. This line went from effectively nil in Fiscal 2024 (0.02 million) to 778.91 million / 19.71% in Fiscal 2025 and 411.11 million / 17.24% in H1FY26. Related-party density runs through both ends of the chain: Sanjoo Dyeing & Printing Mills Private Limited was simultaneously the largest customer (563.88 million / 23.65% of revenue in H1FY26) and the fourth-largest supplier (142.74 million / 8.68% of purchases in H1FY26). Workforce as of September 30, 2025: 213 employees (142 in facility operations, 17 accounts and finance, 16 admin and HR, 8 aviation, 8 management, 7 legal and compliance, 5 each in IT & automation, sales and marketing, and procurement) plus 292 contract labourers (136 Ankleshwar, 50 Nandesari, 34 Sarigam, 38 Vapi, 34 Panoli); attrition 10.12% in H1FY26, 37.83% in Fiscal 2025, 22.74% in Fiscal 2024 and 30.29% in Fiscal 2023. Inventories were 309.16 million at September 30, 2025 (461.02 million at March 31, 2025, 462.27 million at March 31, 2024, 83.18 million at March 31, 2023) with inventory turnover of 5.81 (not annualised), 6.16, 3.89 and 27.33 respectively.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- Leading market position as a community industrial gas provider - pioneer of India's community boiler system (first introduced in 2014) and, per F&S, the market leader in supply of steam through community boilers
- High barriers to entry - exclusive pipeline network already laid inside industrial clusters where limited space prevents a second distribution network being built
- Only company in India supplying nitrogen through a distributed pipeline network rather than cryogenic tanks or onsite generation (Source: F&S Report)
- Sticky, contracted customer base - customer supply arrangements of 12 …

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Every boiler and the nitrogen unit sit in Gujarat and gas can only be supplied to customers close enough to be pipeline-connected, so each facility's addressable market is a single industrial estate; growth depends on finding suitable land next to clusters and on securing and retaining pipeline rights-of-way from regulators, and there is limited physical space left for new pipelines in established estates.
- Top 10 customers were 53.95% of FY25 revenue and 52.83% in H1 FY26 with the largest alone at 23.65% in H1 FY26; contracts run 12 months to 10 years but there were instances of termination by the Company or the customer in FY25, and customers without written agreements buy on an invoice basis with no continuing obligation.
- Transactions with Group Companies were 70.41% of FY25 revenue from operations and 61.72% in H1 FY26; Sanjoo Dyeing is simultaneously a top-10 customer, a top-10 supplier and the owner of the Sachin boilers the Company merely operates, so a large share of reported scale depends on entities controlled by the Promoter and on the continuation of arm's-length terms.
- Coal was 76.19% of FY25 purchases and 77.97% in H1 FY26, sourced largely from Indian importers who buy Indonesian coal, with no long-term supply contracts and no FX hedging; top 10 suppliers were 91.52% of H1 FY26 purchases, so quantity or quality failure directly stops steam production even though price rises are contractually passed through.
- Total borrowings were Rs 2,165.97 million as at September 30, 2025 (net debt/equity 1.42x) against net worth of Rs 1,396.70 million, with capex of Rs 1,055.36 million in FY25 alone and eight further projects planned; finance costs were 5.61% of FY25 revenue, and Rs 1,500.00 million of Fresh Issue proceeds are earmarked to repay debt, after which further expansion still requires debt or equity.
- 148,874,167 Equity Shares (65.88% of paid-up capital) held by the Promoter were pledged as at the UDRHP-I date; the trustee has confirmed release before UDRHP-II filing but the shares must be repledged if the Ascertis Credit (formerly BPEA) debt is not repaid within an agreed timeline.
- The Company has previously operated a boiler before receiving final regulatory approval and received a GPCB show cause notice dated May 15, 2025 for haphazard plastic waste storage, exhaust leakages and a non-operational screw conveyor; boiler licences for the Vapi WTE unit expired on November 27, 2025 with renewal applications pending, and coal-fired operations remain exposed to tighter emission rules or fuel duties.
- Capacity is planned to nearly double from 345 TPH to 675 TPH, yet Pirana and Tarapur did not have all approvals in place as at September 30, 2025, several projects have no customer tie-ups for the steam, funding is unappraised by any bank or independent agency, and utilisation is already only 45.58% (FY25), so delays, cost overruns or unfilled capacity would hit returns.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Expand capacity by setting up new community industrial gas facilities in and outside Gujarat - Nandesari (Phase 2), Jhagadia, Vapi (Phase 3), Dahej SEZ, Ankleshwar (Phase 3), Pirana (Ahmedabad), Panoli (Phase 2) and Tarapur - and participate in tenders for community gas systems in upcoming industrial parks across India
- Scale the asset-light 'purchase and distribution' model by partnering with industrial units that have unused or by-product steam, expanding distribution capacity with relatively lower capital expenditure
- Diversify business offerings - a hybrid own-plus-purchase steam model, …
